reconstructed_theorem_text: Let (Omega,m,mu) be a finite measure space with filtration F, T>0, scalar Brownian motion B with F, and the usual conditions. Here scalar Brownian motion with filtration means centered Gaussian finite-dimensional laws with covariance min(s,t), mu-almost surely continuous paths, strong F-adaptedness, and independence of B(t)-B(s) from F_s for every s<=t. Zero at time zero is part of the scalar law almost surely. Usual conditions mean that every mu-null subset of Omega is in every F_t, and F is right-continuous. A progressive L2 integrand is a real process strongly progressive for F and in L2(mu product lambda_T), where lambda_T is Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,T], transported to NNReal. I_eta denotes its specified continuous completed Ito integral against the given scalar Brownian driver: the canonical limit of elementary integrals, set to zero on its exceptional null set, and held constant after T. Fix a progressive L2 integrand eta on [0,T], deterministic nonnegative times s<=t<=T, a strongly F_s-measurable real random variable w, and a real C with |w(omega)|<=C for every omega. There exists a progressive L2 integrand theta on [0,T] satisfying theta(r,omega)=1_{s<r<=t}*w(omega)*eta(r,omega) for every r>=0 and every omega, and I_theta(T,omega)=w(omega)*(I_eta(t,omega)-I_eta(s,omega)) for mu-almost every omega. No separate sign assumption on C is stated.
objects: Finite measure space, F,T,B, eta, s,t, multiplier w, pointwise bound C, existential theta.
domains: Real scalar processes on NNReal x Omega; w strongly measurable for F_s; s,t nonnegative; C real.
quantifiers: For all admissible data including w and C with pointwise bound, exists one theta satisfying a universal process formula and one terminal a.e. identity.
assumptions: mu finite; T>0; scalar Brownian with F; usual conditions; eta progressive L2; s<=t<=T; strong F_s-measurability of w; all-omega bound |w|<=C.
conclusion: Interval-supported multiplier integrand exists and its terminal Ito integral is w times the Ito increment from s to t, a.e.
scopes: Process identity all r>=0 and all omega; integral identity only at terminal T and mu-a.e.; no simultaneous all-time identity stated.
constant_dependencies: C is supplied and uniform in omega; may depend on w. Theta depends on eta,w,s,t and structure data; no new constant.
